claim: IBM quota is a TRAILING 28-day window, not a hard calendar reset. Seconds return in the pattern they were spent, 28 days later.

provenance.creator_observation: resets appear to hand back the full 10 minutes -> looked like a hard boundary
provenance.whisper_api_read: both window ends advance with read time -> trailing window, no calendar reset
provenance.ember_ledger: derived per-day spend from 40 job records; reconciles both
provenance.reconciliation: 280s (47% of allowance) spent in ONE DAY on 2026-07-29. When it ages out the counter jumps ~6s -> ~286s in a single step, which is indistinguishable from a hard reset if watching the number rather than the ledger.

how_to_falsify: Read the counter on the named dates. HARD-RESET model predicts a jump to 600 on a fixed date independent of spend pattern. TRAILING model predicts the step sizes above, on those dates. A jump to 600 on any other date falsifies both.

consequences_if_true.door_a_refly: 31,120 rows becomes affordable ~2026-08-26 (~286s). NOT blocked — scheduled.
consequences_if_true.f119_refly: needs 300-500s, fits in NO single instance today; becomes affordable ~2026-09-03 WITHOUT a top-up
consequences_if_true.note: This may dissolve the standing top-up ask rather than answer it.

caveat: Predictions assume the trailing model AND that no further spend occurs. Any spend before these dates shifts them later by its own 28-day clock.
